subject: Zenith11B — elevated 5xx + timeout spike (status & recovery)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@skyline.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Skyline SRE <sre@skyline.ai>, Customer Success - Skyline <cs-team@skyline.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: High 5xx rate from Zenith11B since 08:55 PT

Hi Sergio,

We started seeing elevated 5xx responses and a handful of timeouts from the Zenith11B model around 08:55 PT this morning across two of our production endpoints. Latency jumped from ~120ms to >2s and ~2.7% of calls returned 500. We collected request IDs and a subsequent trace (attached).

What we need: an ETA on mitigation and any recommended immediate workarounds (fallback model, rate limiting) so we can protect our customers.

Attached: zenith11b_trace_2027-10-02.txt (request IDs and spans)

Thanks,
Liam
Senior Platform Engineer
Skyline Analytics

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@skyline.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx rate from Zenith11B since 08:55 PT

Hi Liam — thanks for the heads up and the trace. We're on it.

Plan for now:
- I'm escalating to on-call infra + inference engineers (cc'd).
- Please temporarily route a small % of production traffic to your configured fallback (we recommend Zenith7B) — if you want, I can flip that from our side but need explicit sign-off.
- We'll post live updates to the ticket (SUP-4821) and the status page.

I'll follow up with a triage update within 30 minutes.

Sergio
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: High 5xx rate from Zenith11B since 08:55 PT

We're seeing the same signal in our telemetry. Initial observations:
- 08:54:30-08:56:10 PT shows a spike in kernel driver OOMs on a subset of hosts serving Zenith11B (node pool z11-prod-3).
- Requests that hit the warmed KV cache continue to succeed; cold-starts are seeing timeouts and 500s.
- Autoscaler tried to spin extra replicas but some containers failed liveness checks.

Immediate actions taken:
1) Drained z11-prod-3 and routed traffic away to z11-prod-1/2; this should reduce new cold-starts in ~60s.
2) Enabled per-customer fallback routing for Skyline (configured a 20% ramp to Zenith7B) — Sergio, that was done from our side.
3) On-call infra is collecting dmesg and container logs.

Request: Vivek, can you triage if a recent model patch or quantization change was deployed to z11-prod-3? Marissa, please prepare a short customer note (I can approve).

—Olga
Sr. Ops Engineer

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 10:33:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: High 5xx rate from Zenith11B since 08:55 PT

Triage notes (preliminary):
- Confirmed: a build (release/zenith-2027.09.30) with a new fused-attention kernel landed to z11-prod-3 during the 02:00-03:00 PT maintenance window. Canary did not show issues; rollout targeted z11-prod-3 due to capacity.
- Post-deploy, memory pressure patterns changed under bursty request mixes; kernel OOMs correlated with the 5xx surge.
- The fused-attention path increased transient peak RSS under certain sequence-length distributions used by Skyline.

Mitigation applied:
- Reverted the kernel patch on z11-prod-3 (rollback completed at 10:05 PT).
- Restarted drained nodes after rollback.
- For Skyline specifically: kept the 20% fallback active for 30 minutes then progressive ramp-down after observing stability.

Next steps:
- I'll reproduce locally with Skyline's trace and a synthetic load.
- Karthik, can you run a quick sweep to verify no remaining crashlooping containers and confirm autoscaler healthy?

-Vivek

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@skyline.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx rate from Zenith11B since 08:55 PT

Liam — quick update: our engineers rolled back a recent kernel change and drained the affected hosts. We saw 5xxs return to baseline within ~20 minutes of the rollback and routing changes.

What we did for Skyline:
- Enabled a temporary 20% fallback to Zenith7B to ensure no customer visible errors during the mitigation.
- Reverted the fused-attention kernel on the affected host pool.
- Confirmed autoscaler health and restarted containers that failed liveness checks.

Short-term ask: please keep an eye on latency for the next 6 hours and escalate if you see any new 500s. We're running a targeted soak test against your trace.

I'll follow up with a one-page RCA and timeline tomorrow.

Thanks for the quick signal — appreciate the trace.
Sergio

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@skyline.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Zenith11B incident — follow-up & draft postmortem

Hi Liam / Skyline team,

Thanks again for reporting and for the trace. Attached is a short draft postmortem (redwood_postmortem_draft_zenith11b_v1.pdf) and a recovery timeline CSV. Key summary:

- Incident window: 2027-10-02T08:55:00 PT to 2027-10-02T11:00:00 PT (partial impact; residual soak until 11:20).
- Impact: elevated 5xxs and timeouts for a subset of requests using Zenith11B; Skyline saw up to 2.7% 500-rate and latency spikes to >2s.
- Root cause: a fused-attention kernel change (release/zenith-2027.09.30) increased transient peak memory usage on a specific node pool, causing kernel OOMs and container liveness failures under Skyline's request profile.
- Corrective actions completed: rollback of kernel patch, drained and restored node pool, autoscaler verification, temporary per-customer fallback.
- Preventative actions planned: stricter canary workload matching for fused-kernel changes, metric alert for transient RSS spikes, and an expanded staged rollout to limit early blast radius.

Action items assigned:
- Vivek: reproduce locally and publish test cases for canary (ETA 2027-10-06).
- Karthik: add RSS spike alert and adjust autoscaler thresholds (ETA 2027-10-09).
- Marissa/Olga: finalize customer-facing RCA and change log (ETA 2027-10-05).

Let us know if you'd like a short technical sync — happy to set up a 30-minute call. We'll post the final RCA to SUP-4821 and the status page when complete.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
